<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

    "The rounding operations are arbitrary total functions on real pairs satisfying the stated relative-error model. No floating-point format, rounding mode, representable set, overflow behavior, or probabilistic independence is specified.",

  ],

    {
      "effect_on_target": "This is the hypothesis imposed on both rounding functions, with the same uniform error bound u.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For u ∈ ℝ and A, M : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, the predicate asserts both: for every a,b ∈ ℝ there exists δ ∈ ℝ with |δ| ≤ u and A(a,b) = (a+b)(1+δ); and for every a,b ∈ ℝ there exists δ ∈ ℝ with |δ| ≤ u and M(a,b) = ab(1+δ). The witnesses may depend on the operands and on which operation is used.",
      "name": "Uniform relative-error model",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the error coefficient at k = levels·(blockSize−1)+1. The target hypothesis makes its denominator strictly positive.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "For every real u and natural k, define γ_k(u) = ((k : ℝ)u)/(1−(k : ℝ)u). This definition itself has no denominator restriction; Lean real division is total, including division by zero.",
      "name": "Gamma error coefficient",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the computed scalar whose absolute error is bounded.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "Given A,M : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, natural numbers L,b, and x,y : Fin(b^L) → ℝ, form the ordered list [M(x_i,y_i)] for i = 0,…,b^L−1 and apply the recursive reduction of D004 with addition A, block size b, and depth L.",
      "name": "Hierarchically computed dot product",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the precise reduction tree and the contiguous grouping of products. Each level uses a sequential reduction of b child results, giving at most b−1 rounded additions per level along any leaf's path.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For A : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ and b ∈ ℕ, define T_0(v) as the first entry of the real list v, or 0 if v is empty. For ℓ ∈ ℕ, define T_{ℓ+1}(v) = S_A([T_ℓ(take(b^ℓ, drop(j·b^ℓ,v)))]_{j=0}^{b−1}), where S_A is D005. This is defined for every list length and every natural b and depth; slices truncate at the list end, and entries beyond the selected blocks are ignored.",
      "name": "Recursive contiguous-block reduction",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Determines the addition order within each node. A node with b positive-numbered children performs b−1 rounded additions, without an initial rounded addition to zero.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For A : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, S_A([])=0 and S_A(a::v)=foldl(A,a,v). Thus S_A([a₀,…,a_{m−1}]) is the left-associated application of A starting from a₀; a singleton is returned unchanged.",
      "name": "Sequential nonempty-list summation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Selects the depth-zero or successor-depth branch of D004 while keeping its input list fixed.",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For any universe-polymorphic family P : ℕ → List(ℝ) → Sort, n ∈ ℕ, list v, a branch h₀ assigning an element of P(0,w) to every list w, and a branch hₛ assigning an element of P(m+1,w) to every m and w, return h₀(v) when n=0 and hₛ(m,v) when n=m+1. The result has type P(n,v).",
      "name": "Depth case selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Selects the empty and nonempty branches of D005.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For any family P : List(ℝ) → Sort, list v, h₀ : Unit → P([]), and h_c assigning an element of P(a::w) to every real a and real list w, return h₀(()) if v is empty and h_c(a,w) if v=a::w.",
      "name": "Real-list case selector",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes each input vector have exactly blockSize^levels real coordinates.",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For n ∈ ℕ, Fin(n) is the finite type of natural indices i satisfying 0 ≤ i < n.",
      "name": "Bounded natural indices",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Enables summation over every coordinate of the input vectors.",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For each n ∈ ℕ, supplies a finite enumeration of Fin(n) from the list of all its indices, with no duplicates and with every index included.",
      "name": "Finite enumeration of bounded indices",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Both the reference dot product and the sum of absolute products use exact finite real summation.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "For arbitrary types I and M, an additive commutative monoid structure on M, a finite subset s of I, and f : I → M, define ∑_{i∈s} f(i) by mapping f over the underlying multiset and summing it. The empty sum is zero.",
      "name": "Finite-set sum",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Ensures that neither sum omits any index in Fin(blockSize^levels).",
      "id": "D011",
      "meaning": "For any type α equipped with a finite enumeration, univ is the finite set containing every element of α.",
      "name": "Universal finite set",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Interprets addition in the natural error-count expression and the exact real expressions in the rounding model.",

      "name": "Addition operation projection",

    },

      "meaning": "For types α,β,γ and a heterogeneous multiplication structure HMul(α,β,γ), returns its operation α × β → γ.",
      "name": "Multiplication operation projection",

  "role": "blind-translation",
  "semantic_sha256": "59a03e84f4317ecb81f46adce83009b757e2e40b01db3812a0fee008d26f2ca0",
  "translation": {
    "binders": [
      "Universally quantify levels L ∈ ℕ and blockSize b ∈ ℕ.",
      "Assume hlevels : 0 < L and hblock : 0 < b.",
      "Universally quantify u ∈ ℝ and assume hu : 0 ≤ u.",
      "Universally quantify roundAdd A : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ and roundMul M : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ.",
      "Assume hround: A and M satisfy the uniform relative-error model with bound u.",
      "Assume hgamma: ((L·(b−1)+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)u < 1.",
      "For these choices, universally quantify x,y : Fin(b^L) → ℝ."
    ],
    "conclusions": [
      "Writing N=b^L, k=L·(b−1)+1, and D̂=T_L([M(x_i,y_i)]_{i=0}^{N−1}), the conclusion is |D̂−∑_{i=0}^{N−1}x_i y_i| ≤ ((k : ℝ)u/(1−(k : ℝ)u))·∑_{i=0}^{N−1}|x_i y_i|."
    ],
    "hypotheses": [
      "L and b are strictly positive natural numbers.",
      "u is a nonnegative real number.",
      "For every a,b' ∈ ℝ, there exists a real δ_A depending on these operands such that |δ_A| ≤ u and A(a,b')=(a+b')(1+δ_A).",
      "For every a,b' ∈ ℝ, there exists a real δ_M depending on these operands such that |δ_M| ≤ u and M(a,b')=ab'(1+δ_M). These witnesses are separate from the addition witnesses.",
      "For the natural number k=L·(b−1)+1, its real cast satisfies ku<1. The subtraction b−1 is natural truncated subtraction; b>0 makes it ordinary subtraction here.",
      "The inputs x and y are arbitrary real-valued functions on the N=b^L indices. No sign, magnitude, nonzero-coordinate, or nonzero-dot-product restriction is imposed."
    ],
    "mathematical_definitions": [
      "Fin(N) consists of indices 0,…,N−1. All sums in the conclusion are exact real sums over this entire finite index set.",
      "Define S_A([])=0 and S_A([a₀,…,a_{m−1}]) by left-folding A through the entries after a₀ with initial accumulator a₀. In particular S_A([a₀])=a₀.",
      "For fixed A and b, define T_0(v)=headD(v,0), the first entry of v or zero if empty.",
      "For ℓ ∈ ℕ, define T_{ℓ+1}(v)=S_A([T_ℓ(take(b^ℓ,drop(j·b^ℓ,v)))]_{j=0}^{b−1}). The children are ordered by increasing j, and each slice is a consecutive block.",
      "The computed dot product first makes the list of rounded products M(x_i,y_i) in increasing index order and then applies T_L. It performs one rounded multiplication per coordinate and sequential rounded additions within every recursive node.",
      "Define γ_k(u)=((k : ℝ)u)/(1−(k : ℝ)u). In the target, k≥1 and 0≤ku<1, so the denominator is positive and γ_k(u)≥0.",
      "Absolute value is |a|=max(a,−a). The factor ∑|x_i y_i| is the sum of absolute coordinatewise products, equivalently the ℓ¹ norm of their product vector."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every positive natural depth L and positive natural block size b, every nonnegative real error bound u, and every pair of total real addition and multiplication functions satisfying the stated relative-error model, if (L(b−1)+1)u<1, then for every two real vectors of length b^L the recursively grouped dot product defined above has absolute forward error at most γ_{L(b−1)+1}(u) times the sum of the absolute exact coordinate products. The algorithm groups consecutive entries into b equal subblocks recursively and combines each node's b results by sequential left-associated rounded addition starting from its first result."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "The hypotheses are satisfiable: for any positive L and b, exact real addition and multiplication satisfy the model with δ=0, and u=0 satisfies every numerical hypothesis. There is no global contradiction or universal vacuity.",
    "For choices with L=0, b=0, u<0, ku≥1, or rounding functions violating the model, the conditional proposition provides no error guarantee.",
    "The input index set is nonempty because b>0 implies b^L≥1. On the specified input length, the recursive slices have their required lengths, so empty-list fallbacks do not trivialize the target.",
    "The allowed case b=1 has N=1 and k=1 for every positive L. Every reduction node returns its sole child unchanged, and the target bounds only the one rounded multiplication.",

    "If ∑|x_i y_i|=0, every exact coordinate product is zero. The relative-error model forces those rounded products and their subsequent sums to be zero, so the conclusion becomes 0≤0.",
    "The model forces an exactly zero result whenever the corresponding exact sum or product is zero. Its uniform applicability to all real operands is a substantive assumption; no concrete machine implementation is asserted to satisfy it."
  ]

    "mathematical_definitions": [

      "Define S_A([])=0 and S_A([a₀,…,a_{m−1}]) by left-folding A through the entries after a₀ with initial accumulator a₀. In particular S_A([a₀])=a₀.",
      "For fixed A and b, define T_0(v)=headD(v,0), the first entry of v or zero if empty.",
      "For ℓ ∈ ℕ, define T_{ℓ+1}(v)=S_A([T_ℓ(take(b^ℓ,drop(j·b^ℓ,v)))]_{j=0}^{b−1}). The children are ordered by increasing j, and each slice is a consecutive block.",
      "The computed dot product first makes the list of rounded products M(x_i,y_i) in increasing index order and then applies T_L. It performs one rounded multiplication per coordinate and sequential rounded additions within every recursive node.",
      "Define γ_k(u)=((k : ℝ)u)/(1−(k : ℝ)u). In the target, k≥1 and 0≤ku<1, so the denominator is positive and γ_k(u)≥0.",
      "Absolute value is |a|=max(a,−a). The factor ∑|x_i y_i| is the sum of absolute coordinatewise products, equivalently the ℓ¹ norm of their product vector."
    ],
    "proposition_plain_english": "For every positive natural depth L and positive natural block size b, every nonnegative real error bound u, and every pair of total real addition and multiplication functions satisfying the stated relative-error model, if (L(b−1)+1)u<1, then for every two real vectors of length b^L the recursively grouped dot product defined above has absolute forward error at most γ_{L(b−1)+1}(u) times the sum of the absolute exact coordinate products. The algorithm groups consecutive entries into b equal subblocks recursively and combines each node's b results by sequential left-associated rounded addition starting from its first result."
  },
  "vacuity_risks": [
    "The hypotheses are satisfiable: for any positive L and b, exact real addition and multiplication satisfy the model with δ=0, and u=0 satisfies every numerical hypothesis. There is no global contradiction or universal vacuity.",
    "For choices with L=0, b=0, u<0, ku≥1, or rounding functions violating the model, the conditional proposition provides no error guarantee.",
    "The input index set is nonempty because b>0 implies b^L≥1. On the specified input length, the recursive slices have their required lengths, so empty-list fallbacks do not trivialize the target.",
    "The allowed case b=1 has N=1 and k=1 for every positive L. Every reduction node returns its sole child unchanged, and the target bounds only the one rounded multiplication.",
    "When u=0, the model forces both operations to be exact and the conclusion has zero right-hand side.",
    "If ∑|x_i y_i|=0, every exact coordinate product is zero. The relative-error model forces those rounded products and their subsequent sums to be zero, so the conclusion becomes 0≤0.",
    "The model forces an exactly zero result whenever the corresponding exact sum or product is zero. Its uniform applicability to all real operands is a substantive assumption; no concrete machine implementation is asserted to satisfy it."
  ]
}
